name: Salvia nemorosa
description: A clump-forming perennial sage with dense spikes of violet-blue flowers over purple bracts in summer and autumn. It is drought tolerant once established and attracts bees and butterflies.

name: Salvia greggii
description: A small, semi-woody sage from Texas and Mexico with two-lipped red, pink or white flowers from spring to autumn. It needs well-drained soil and tolerates rocky ground.
edible: leaves as a seasoning or tea, and flowers

name: Salvia farinacea
description: A tender perennial sage with long spikes of small violet-blue flowers and mealy white hairs on the flower stems, from spring to autumn. It is often grown as an annual.

name: Salvia splendens
description: A tender Brazilian sage grown as a bedding annual, with spikes of scarlet or other coloured flowers from spring to autumn. It needs warmth and is not drought tolerant.

name: Stachys byzantina
description: A soft groundcover with woolly, silver leaves and spikes of small pink-purple flowers in summer. It needs very well-drained soil and dislikes humid summers.
care_note: Please avoid overwatering, because wet leaves invite disease.

name: Ajuga reptans
description: An evergreen groundcover with spikes of blue-violet flowers in spring and summer. It makes a thick carpet in cool, shady spots where grass will not grow.
care_note: It spreads readily and can become weedy. Please avoid wet, heavy soil.

name: Coleus scutellarioides
description: A mounding plant grown for its brightly patterned leaves, often as an annual. It grows best in moist, rich soil in part shade and wilts quickly when dry.

toxic.note: Repeated handling can give some people an itchy skin rash. Please wear gloves if your skin reacts.

name: Nepeta × faassenii
description: A sterile catmint that forms a spreading clump of aromatic grey-green leaves with violet-blue flower spikes from spring into summer. Cats are drawn to its scent.
pruning: Shear after flowering to bring on another flush.

name: Agastache foeniculum
description: An upright perennial with anise-scented leaves and spikes of small blue to purple flowers in summer and autumn that draw bees and butterflies.

name: Lavandula × intermedia
description: A hybrid of English and Portuguese lavender that grows larger than either parent, with long, very fragrant flower spikes in summer.

name: Leucanthemum × superbum
description: An old-fashioned border perennial with large white daisies with yellow centres in spring and summer. They are good for cutting.

toxic.note: Eating it can cause mouth irritation, vomiting and diarrhoea, and the sap can irritate skin. Please wear gloves if your skin reacts, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 if a child eats some.

name: Gaillardia × grandiflora
description: A short-lived perennial with large daisies in red, orange and yellow through summer. It copes with dry soil and salt, and keeps flowering if deadheaded.
care_note: It needs good drainage and may not survive winter in poorly drained clay.

name: Rudbeckia hirta
description: A fast-growing biennial or short-lived perennial with golden-yellow to orange daisies with dark centres in spring and summer. It flowers in its first year from seed and lasts well as a cut flower.

name: Tagetes erecta
description: A tender annual marigold from Mexico with large flower heads in yellow, orange, cream or red through summer and autumn.

toxic.note: The sap can cause redness and blisters on skin that is then exposed to sunlight. Please wear gloves when handling it.

name: Hemerocallis fulva
description: A tough, clump-forming perennial with arching leaves and orange trumpet flowers in summer, each lasting a single day. The buds and flowers are edible for people.

toxic.note: Every part, even the pollen, can cause fatal kidney failure in cats, and a small amount is enough. Please keep cats away from it, and take a cat to a vet at once if it may have eaten any.

name: Aloe vera
description: A stemless succulent with a rosette of thick, fleshy leaves and spikes of yellow to orange flowers in winter and spring.

toxic.note: Eating the leaves can cause stomach cramps and diarrhoea, and the sap can irritate skin. Please keep children from chewing it, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 if any is eaten.

name: Kniphofia uvaria
description: A clumping perennial from South Africa with tall spikes of red, yellow and cream flowers like flaming torches in summer.

name: Liriope muscari
description: A clumping evergreen with narrow, arching dark green leaves and spikes of small purple flowers in late summer and early autumn. It makes a tough edging or groundcover in sun or shade.

name: Aspidistra elatior
description: A tough evergreen with upright, dark green leaves that grows in dense shade, outdoors or in a pot indoors.

name: Crassula ovata
description: A succulent shrub from South Africa with thick, egg-shaped leaves that slowly grows into a miniature tree. Small pink or white flowers appear in spring.

toxic.note: It can make cats and dogs sick if they chew it. Please keep pets away from it, and call a vet if a pet eats some.

name: Echeveria elegans
description: A clumping rosette succulent from Mexico with arching stalks of pink, orange or yellow flowers from late winter into spring.

name: Kalanchoe blossfeldiana
description: A compact flowering succulent from Madagascar with glossy, scalloped leaves and dense clusters of red, orange, yellow, pink or white flowers in winter and spring.

toxic.note: Every part contains heart poisons that can cause vomiting, diarrhoea and an irregular heartbeat, and they can kill pets. Please keep it away from children and pets, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26, or a vet for a pet, if any is eaten.

name: Hylotelephium telephium
description: An upright succulent perennial with fleshy leaves and flat heads of pink, purple, red or white flowers in summer and autumn that bees and butterflies visit.

name: Portulaca grandiflora
description: A low annual from South America with fleshy, narrow leaves and bright single or double flowers in many colours from spring to autumn. The flowers stay closed on cloudy days.

name: Iris germanica
description: A rhizomatous perennial with sword-shaped leaves and large bearded flowers in almost every colour.

toxic.note: The rhizomes, seeds and sap can cause nausea and vomiting if eaten, and the sap can irritate skin. Please wear gloves when dividing clumps, and keep pets from chewing the rhizomes.

name: Rhododendron indicum
description: A compact, semi-evergreen azalea from Japan with pink or red flowers in spring and often again in autumn.

toxic.note: Every part contains grayanotoxins. A small taste is unlikely to harm, but please keep children and pets from eating it, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26, or a vet for a pet, if a lot is eaten.

name: Hydrangea paniculata
description: A large shrub or small tree with cone-shaped heads of white flowers in summer and autumn that age to pink or brown.

name: Buxus microphylla
description: A small-leaved evergreen box from Japan, widely used for low hedges and topiary.

toxic.note: Eating the leaves or bark can cause nausea and diarrhoea, and the sap can irritate skin. Please wear gloves when clipping it, and keep children and pets from chewing it.

name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
description: A shrub from Mexico grown for its large red, and sometimes yellow, leaf-like bracts in winter and spring.

toxic.note: The milky sap in every part can irritate skin and damage the eyes. Please wear gloves and eye protection when pruning it, and keep children and pets from chewing it.

name: Codiaeum variegatum
description: A tropical shrub grown for its bold, variegated leaves, often kept in a pot or indoors.

toxic.note: The sap can irritate skin, and eating a large amount causes vomiting and diarrhoea. Please wear gloves when pruning it.

name: Nerium oleander
description: A fast-growing evergreen shrub with narrow leaves and clusters of white, pink, salmon or apricot flowers from late spring to late summer. It tolerates drought, salt, wind and poor soil, but every part is very poisonous.

toxic.note: Every part is highly poisonous, fresh or dry, and eating it can be fatal. The sap also irritates skin. Please keep children and pets away from it, and call 000 or the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 at once if any is eaten.

name: Trachelospermum asiaticum
description: A fast-growing evergreen groundcover or climber with glossy leaves and fragrant cream to yellow star flowers in spring and summer. As a groundcover it stays low and spreads 3 metres or more.

name: Pentas lanceolata
description: A tropical shrubby perennial with rounded clusters of small starry flowers in pink, red, purple or white through summer and autumn. Butterflies love it.

name: Ixora coccinea
description: A compact tropical shrub with leathery, dark green leaves and dense, rounded clusters of red flowers in summer.

name: Osmanthus fragrans
description: A dense evergreen shrub from China and Japan whose small white flowers are extremely fragrant in early spring and again in autumn.

name: Antirrhinum majus
description: A short-lived perennial grown as an annual, with spikes of snout-shaped flowers in many colours from spring to autumn.
care_note: Please water the soil rather than the leaves.

name: Angelonia angustifolia
description: A bushy tropical perennial with long spikes of small, two-lipped flowers in blue, purple, pink or white through summer and autumn. It copes with heat and dry soil.

name: Brunfelsia pauciflora
description: A bushy shrub whose fragrant flowers open deep purple and fade to lavender and then white, so all three colours show at once in spring and summer.

toxic.note: It is poisonous and can cause vomiting, tremors and seizures in dogs and cats, and the sap can irritate skin and eyes. Please keep pets and children away from it, and call a vet or the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 if any is eaten.

name: Zamioculcas zamiifolia
description: A slow-growing plant from tropical Africa with upright stems of glossy leaflets rising from a thick rhizome. It copes with low light and drought, indoors or out.

toxic.note: Eating a lot of the leaves can cause vomiting and diarrhoea. Please keep cats and dogs from chewing it.

name: Thaumatophyllum xanadu
description: A clumping philodendron from southern Brazil and Paraguay, grown outdoors in warm gardens or as a houseplant.

toxic.note: Chewing the leaves or stems makes the lips, tongue and mouth swell painfully, and the sap irritates skin. Please keep children and pets from chewing it.

name: Ficus lyrata
description: A tropical tree with large, lyre-shaped leaves up to 45 cm long, usually grown as a houseplant or in a warm, sheltered garden.

toxic.note: Chewing the leaves burns the mouth and can cause drooling and vomiting. Please keep children and pets from chewing them.

name: Strelitzia nicolai
description: A giant clumping plant from southern Africa with large, banana-like grey-green leaves. Its blue and white flowers sit in purplish-black, beak-like bracts in spring.

toxic.note: Eating the fruit or seeds can cause stomach cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea, and the sap can irritate skin. Please keep children and pets from eating the seeds.

name: Tibouchina urvilleana
description: An evergreen shrub from Brazil with large purple flowers from spring to autumn. It can be trained into a small tree.

name: Photinia × fraseri
description: A large evergreen shrub or small tree, widely grown as a hedge for its red new growth, with clusters of white flowers in spring.

name: Bauhinia × blakeana
description: A spreading, semi-evergreen tree with large, orchid-like flowers in reddish-purple to pink from autumn to spring.

name: Pelargonium peltatum
description: A trailing pelargonium from South Africa with shield-shaped leaves and clusters of pink, red or white flowers in summer.

toxic.note: Eating a lot can upset the stomach of cats and dogs, and the sap can irritate skin. Please keep pets from chewing it.

name: Impatiens hawkeri
description: A bushy annual from New Guinea and the Solomon Islands with large flowers in orange, pink, purple, red or white from spring to autumn.

name: Hibiscus syriacus
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub from China with large hibiscus flowers in pink, purple, white or yellow through spring and summer.
care_note: It can self-seed and become weedy.

name: Alcea rosea
description: A tall biennial with spires of large flowers in many colours from spring to autumn, visited by bees and butterflies.

name: Viola × wittrockiana
description: A popular cool-season bedding plant with flat flowers in many colours and patterns from autumn to spring.

name: Lobularia maritima
description: A mat-forming annual or short-lived perennial with spreading mounds of small, fragrant white or purple flowers from spring to autumn. It draws predatory insects that help control pests.

name: Nemesia strumosa
description: A bright annual from southern Africa with flowers in yellow, orange, pink, cream, red, mauve or white. It flowers best in mild weather.
